title: Texas's 24th Congressional District Election, 2026
description: This is the general election for Texas's 24th Congressional District, covering portions of Dallas and Tarrant counties. Incumbent Republican Representative Beth Van Duyne is seeking a fourth term against Democratic nominee Kevin Burge, a U.S. Marine Corps veteran and former intelligence professional. The district was significantly redrawn in 2021 to favor Republicans, and the Cook Political Report rates the race as 'Solidly Republican.' Van Duyne won her previous two elections in the redrawn district by approximately 20-point margins, making Burge a long-shot challenger in this suburban Dallas-Fort Worth seat.

candidates.name: Beth Van Duyne
candidates.summary: Beth Van Duyne is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Texas's 24th Congressional District, first elected in 2020. She previously served as mayor of Irving, Texas from 2011 to 2017 and as a regional administrator for the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development during the first Trump administration. Van Duyne is a conservative Republican who has supported Trump-endorsed policies and voted to object to Pennsylvania's electoral votes in the 2020 presidential election.

candidates.name: Kevin Burge
candidates.summary: Kevin Burge is a U.S. Marine Corps veteran who served two deployments to Iraq and one to Afghanistan, and later worked as a technical advisor in the White House Situation Room during the Biden administration. He is the Democratic nominee for Texas's 24th Congressional District after winning the May 2026 primary runoff. His campaign focuses on affordable housing, Medicare for All, immigration reform, restoring abortion rights, and tuition-free public college and trade education.

forecast.rationale: There are no public polls available for this race, so the forecast relies entirely on district fundamentals, which strongly favor the incumbent Republican. Beth Van Duyne is a three-term incumbent in a district that was significantly redrawn in 2021 to favor Republicans, and she has won her previous two elections in the redrawn district by approximately 20-point margins. Cook Political Report rates the seat 'Solidly Republican.' Kevin Burge is a credible Democratic nominee (Marine Corps veteran, former White House Situation Room advisor), but in this heavily Republican-leaning district he remains a clear long-shot. The win probability of 0.97 reflects an overwhelming Republican advantage consistent with the 'safe_r' rating band (95%+). However, confidence is medium rather than high due to the complete absence of polling data and the possibility that district dynamics could shift by November.
